impact:
Running `combined --since <week>` on the maintainer's real data shows ~35 rows like `-private-var-folders-…-T-t009-client-cwd-<rand>` at $0.05–$0.29 each — temp working directories created by our own T-009 spike's client tests, each rendered as a distinct "project". Harmless to totals (~$5 of $23.6k) but visually dominant: they outnumber real projects 2:1 in the table.

The oracle collapses ~/Desktop/scratchpad-style paths but not /private/var/folders/**/T/** (macOS $TMPDIR). The v0.x CLI is byte-frozen to usage.py, so any CLI-side collapse needs an ALLOWLIST entry — OR this lands as presentation logic in the v0.3 menubar UI, which is not parity-bound. Decide placement when the UI work starts; the UI route avoids touching the frozen renderer entirely.
title: Temp-dir cwds pollute per-project tables (dogfooding find)
